event_date_basis: Coinbase's Super Bowl LVI broadcast commercial on 13 February 2022. The American sports bar is a fictional viewing scene, not a documented venue or an advertisement on a stadium screen.

clue_crops.verified_pixels: One black-and-white QR on a white quadrilateral within the television; no phone or duplicate phone preview.

clue_crops.label: sparse black television screen
clue_crops.verified_pixels: Broad black area left of the QR, bounded by the television frame; no text, corner-bounce trail or extra on-screen message.

clue_crops.label: opposing fan colours
clue_crops.verified_pixels: Blue/gold shirts at left and black/orange shirts at right. Fan-shirt and hat emblems were removed in final v17; visible shirt numbers remain.

clue_crops.verified_pixels: Brown football with light laces inside a clear rectangular case under the television; no readable signature or provenance label.

retrieval_limitations: Traffic is Coinbase's first-party report, not an audited count of people or customers.
The agency case study has no displayed publication date; format details are cross-checked with contemporary Clio reporting.
The original Coinbase YouTube asset could not be retrieved. Duration is supported by the campaign agency; screen behaviour by contemporary reporting.

Independent QR decoding was not rerun because this authoring environment lacked decoder modules. Existing v17 decode evidence and exact build URLs were inspected. Release-level QR and route QA remain with the publishing worker.
This task checks copy and asset identity only; it does not certify book layout, print readability, repository integration, live publication or physical scanning.
release_guardrails: Keep COMMON / 13 FEB 2022 / COINBASE / THE BOUNCING QR / SUPER BOWL LVI.
Keep the day-precision broadcast event date. The bar is fictional; do not imply an in-stadium video-board advert.
Attribute the more-than-20-million one-minute landing-page-hit metric to Coinbase; never substitute customers, unique people, accounts or completed scans.
Distinguish the original colourful animated QR from this still artwork's replacement black-and-white code.
TV QR is public digital /scan/076/; footer is /crypto/076/. Neither is Coinbase's original signup destination.
No physical-only code or secret exists. Do not invent one, repurpose the public code as one, or suggest the variant split is already implemented.
Use digital art in public books/assets. Any future physical-only master or destination needs separate approval and an appropriately private destination.
Physical/private implementation details stay in the production audit, not public-facing book prose.
Make no claim that any route, puzzle, prize, reward, promotion or ownership check is live or available.
Use only actual final-image clues. There is no phone, QR miniature, moving-square trail, overloaded doorway or listing programme.
Rams blue/gold and Bengals black/orange are fan colours, not exact game uniforms. Do not restore removed shirt/hat emblems.
Bar, people, decor and football case are editorial inventions; no real spectator, signed ball or particular venue is identified.
